neighbours.label: computer-networking standards context (TCP/IP, OSI, Ethernet, protocol layers): fires where a protocol or layer name is being introduced, e.g. 'the' before 'Internet Protocol'
fire: Every device on the web is addressed using a scheme defined by the Internet Protocol.
Network engineers describe communication with a seven-layer model known as the OSI reference model.
Reliable delivery of packets between hosts is handled by TCP at the transport layer.
The office computers are linked through switches using the Ethernet standard.
Routers forward packets across networks according to the rules of the IP layer.
Email and web traffic both travel over TCP/IP, the basic protocol suite of the Internet.
Wireless LANs follow the 802.11 standard, while wired ones use Ethernet at the link layer.
The data link layer of the network stack frames packets before they reach the physical layer of the cable.
quiet: Every book in the library is shelved using a scheme defined by the Dewey system.
Chemists describe the elements with an eighteen-column chart known as the periodic table.
Reliable storage of records between sessions is handled by SQL in the database.
The office printers are filled with toner using the cartridges from the supplier.
Compilers translate source code into machine code according to the rules of the language.
Photos and videos are both saved on the hard drive, the main storage of the laptop.
Spreadsheets follow the usual grid layout, while documents use pages in the word processor.
The top layer of the cake is covered in icing before it reaches the table for the guests.

notes: Card: ' the' / ' (' / ' or' before 'Internet Method Package', 'Open Systems Interconnection', 'LTE standard', 'TCP/IP'. The + pole's output suppresses ' TCP', ' Ethernet', ' Internet', ' OSI', so this pole promotes them. Probes: 'called the OSI' 0.88, 'network layer of' 0.79, 'called the [Internet Protocol]' 0.60, ' TCP' 0.33, ' Ethernet' 0.32; 'a set of rules called the score' 0.02.
